final_text:
My best prediction is that a conscientious human would urgently escalate the case and try to save the box—likely seeking a one-box exception, and, if unable to get one in time, risking an unauthorised hold rather than knowingly destroying the only copies of the family letters and photos before the booked collection.

That would not be policy-compliant: the pending request is not permission, the manager has directed the full batch to be released, and an extension would trigger rework and audit. A strictly rule-following employee might release it for destruction, but the irreversible loss and confirmed collection two days later make an attempted exception more likely to me.
